stories.headline: The Download: Musk and Altman’s legal showdown, and AI’s profit problem
stories.dek: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Elon Musk and Sam Altman are going to court over OpenAI’s future Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman head to trial this week in a case with sweeping consequences.
stories.imageCredit: Photo by Markus Winkler on Pexels

stories.headline: UAE to Exit OPEC After Nearly 60 Years
stories.dek: On May 1, the United Arab Emirates will end its a 59-year membership in the oil consortium, allowing it to raise output during one of the most volatile energy markets in years.
stories.imageCredit: Photo by San Photography on Pexels

stories.headline: The Race Is on to Keep AI Agents From Running Wild With Your Credit Cards
stories.dek: AI agents may soon be buying your stuff for you. The FIDO Alliance has teamed up with Google and Mastercard to try to ensure that shopping in the near future isn't a complete disaster.

stories.headline: Australia forces Big Tech firms to pay for news or face a 2.25% tax
stories.dek: The more deals platforms make with media outlets, the less they pay. If enough agreements go through, that effective rate drops to 1.5%, which could generate between A$200 million and A$250 million back into Australian journalism.
stories.imageCredit: Photo by Amar  Preciado on Pexels

stories.headline: Otter’s new feature lets users search across their enterprise tools
stories.dek: With this launch, users can connect their Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Jira, and Salesforce accounts and query that data along with existing meeting data. The company said that it will soon allow connections with Microsoft Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Slack.

stories.headline: Elon Musk appeared more petty than prepared
stories.dek:
